text:
Does your heart not often flee, Agatha, far from you,
far from the black ocean of the filthy city,
toward another ocean where splendor suddenly bursts forth,
blue, profound, clear as virginity?
Does your heart not often flee, Agatha, far from you?

The sea, the boundless sea, consoles our toil!
What demon endowed the sea, that hoarse singer
seconded by the mighty organ of the winds,
with the sublime office of cradling our dreams?
The sea, the boundless sea, consoles our toil!

Carry me off, frigate! Drag me away, train!
Far away! Here tears have turned to mud!
Is it not true that Agatha’s heart often says:
Far from crimes, from pain and guilt,
carry me off, frigate! Drag me away, train!

How far away you are now, fragrant paradise,
where beneath the heavens all is love and laughter,
where what one loves is worthy of love,
where the heart drowns in pure delight!
How far away you are now, fragrant paradise!

But that paradise of youthful loves,
the races, songs, kisses, and flowers,
violins sounding behind the hills,
and jugs of wine at night in the thicket—
but that paradise of youthful loves,

Innocent paradise of furtive pleasures,
is it farther away than India and China?
Can we call it back with plaintive cries
and still revive it with a silvery voice,
that innocent paradise of furtive pleasures?

translation.title: Mœsta et Errabunda
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The Latin title is retained, and the refrains and apostrophe to Agatha are preserved.
